Type: Artifact
Current Holder: @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.v85bRcnzMrFiDdn6]{The Nodrum} (contained)
First Appeared: @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.jir5X1jFd08ME0H1]{Session 2}

Description

An emanation of the God of Forgetting — a physical manifestation of divine power that emerged during the @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.miGdMuBQ4kTeRR0J]{Godstorm}.
Currently pushed back to a faint outline barely touching reality after the party's intervention at @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.v85bRcnzMrFiDdn6]{The Nodrum}.

Properties

The Xan-Kor can erase things from existence — not merely destroying them, but removing them backward through time, undoing their actions and influence.
It was used during the old wars to erase a champion of @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.Iz0ZE5ZJtcXABZl7]{Lucifer}, undoing a pivotal victory and prolonging the conflict.

History

Imprisoned in the Aurelion Vault (now @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.v85bRcnzMrFiDdn6]{The Nodrum}) after @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.Iz0ZE5ZJtcXABZl7]{Lucifer}'s champion defeated it in a decisive battle — a battle made possible because the God of Forgetting's power had already waned as worshippers turned to the New Gods.
@UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.Pom8bgcTgRw75seF]{The Triune} attempted to reprogram it as the "Aegis Mechanism" for defensive purposes, powering it with energy siphoned from @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.crg1JpVHgdUHPdOO]{Castor}'s curse.
When the party arrived carrying ruin's influence, the containment destabilized and the Xan-Kor began phasing into reality.
The party redirected ley line energy into the @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.pbvNoEuQV2PoM8wM]{Whiteglass} seal, pushing the construct back — but the corrupted ley lines passing through @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.6Eqkl1MNE1055IJC]{Edric} and @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.s4ABoIqxcgBnmTYz]{Roderic} caused reality to shift, retroactively undoing historical events.
